scenes.heading: The Richmack Improvement Formula
scenes.narration: The Richmack Improvement Formula models capability as compound growth created by meaningful stable repetitions.

scenes.heading: The Seven-Rep Rule
scenes.subheading: Seven stable reps model one doubling.
scenes.narration: The core model says that capability doubles after every seven stable repetitions.

scenes.heading: 14 Stable Reps
scenes.narration: Fourteen stable repetitions represent two doublings, which gives a modeled four times improvement.

scenes.heading: Raw Reps vs Stable Reps
scenes.narration: Raw volume is not the goal. A repetition matters when the lesson stabilizes, connects to previous knowledge, and becomes reusable.

scenes.heading: The Learning Loop
scenes.narration: The practical loop is simple. Do the work, write the lesson, refresh what you already learned, and repeat.

scenes.heading: Turn Experience Into Capability
scenes.narration: Improvement comes from what becomes stable enough to reuse, not simply from the amount of activity performed.
